fr.elements: Main Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Driveway; Internal Drive Aisle; Landscaped Area; Front Entry Area; Pedestrian Walkways; Street Frontage; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation; Vehicle Congestion
fr.recommendations: Based on the observed site characteristics, maintaining clear internal drive aisles and coordinating vehicle parking management during incidents could improve apparatus movement and reduce congestion that may otherwise impede responder access. The availability of multiple access points along the street frontage may support multi-unit response staging, though personnel should be aware that rear access appears limited, which could affect positioning for operations on that side of the structure. Dense vegetation and landscaped areas near the front entry and pedestrian walkways may reduce visibility for approaching responders, and managing growth in those areas could enhance situational awareness and navigation throughout the property.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Irrigated Landscape; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Defensible Space; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Adjacent to Access Route; Open Fuel Break
wildfire.recommendations: Maintaining separation between scattered trees and tree clusters from structures and other improvements would support defensible space and may reduce fuel continuity across the property. Managing vegetation observed directly adjacent to structures, including shrubs and mixed vegetation cover, could reduce fuel concentrations near improvements and improve the immediate structure perimeter. Preserving and expanding the existing open fuel break and irrigated landscape areas may further reduce opportunities for fire spread and support long-term wildfire resilience. Thinning or spacing vegetation along the access route could improve driveway navigability and support firefighter access and suppression operations. Addressing limited rear access by clearing vegetation and maintaining adequate clearance along that perimeter would support responder movement and staging around the full structure perimeter. Continued long-term management of scattered shrubs and mixed vegetation cover throughout the property could improve overall defensible space and reduce fuel continuity between vegetation zones.
